images.text:
Vanessa: Michelle, there's been something on my mind I wanted to ask you about.
Michelle: What can I do for you, Vanessa?
Vanessa: My friends just got back from a camping trip, which they said was awesome. They told me that the sky was full of stars. I was wondering, why is it that we don't see many stars here in the city?
Michelle: I asked my friend Josh, who I think is a great source of knowledge, the same question. We both have no doubt that it's because of light pollution. In the cities, we emit lots of light at night, which makes it difficult to see stars that aren't as bright. I'm convinced that's the reason anyway.

Vanessa: Really? So you're saying the brighter the city, the harder it is to see the stars?
Michelle: Correct. The few stars that you can actually see are very bright in comparison to the faint ones, which are seen from darker places.
Vanessa: Oh, that makes sense! I'm going tonight with a friend who I love stargazing with. Do you know of a good place to go?
Michelle: You should go to this really cool place which is just an hour away. I'm sure that you can see the stars that you can't usually see in the city.

Vanessa: Okay. That's awesome! What do you recommend I take with me?
Michelle: I am passionate about identifying the stars so you can take binoculars, which help you find the specific stars and constellations. Other than that, enjoy the experience!
Vanessa: Thanks. Hey, why don't you come with us too! I'm convinced that it's going to be an epic experience, which we will definitely remember for a long time.
Michelle: There's no doubt in my mind that you are right! Okay, I would love to! Let's go!

You can use relative clauses to give more information about a noun. These are sometimes called adjective clauses as well.
A relative clause is a dependent clause and cannot be a complete sentence by itself.
You should go to this really cool place. (Independent Clause) It is just an hour away. (Independent Clause)
You should go to this really cool place (Independent Clause) which is just an hour away. (Dependent Clause)
There are two different types of Relative Clauses:
Defining Relative Clause: this contains information that is necessary to defining or identifying which particular noun you are talking about. You don't use commas with defining relative clauses.

I asked the same question to my friend who/whom I think is a great source of knowledge.
        Something's been on my mind that I wanted to ask you about.

If you don't say “who I think is a great source of knowledge”, then we don't know which friend you are talking about.
If you don't say "that I wanted to ask you about", then we don't know what's on your mind.
In defining relative clauses, who and which can be replaced by that.
Non-Defining Relative Clause: you use this to add extra information about a noun. This is not necessary to identifying the noun. You need to put commas with non-defining relative clauses.
My friends just got back from a camping trip, which they said was awesome.

It is clear which camping trip you mean, so “which they said was awesome” is extra information.
        In non-defining relative clauses, who and which cannot be replaced by that.
I'm going tonight with a friend who I love stargazing with.
I think it's going to be an epic experience, which we will definitely remember for a long time.
Something's been on my mind that I wanted to ask you about.

Everyone has opinions. In discussions or conversation, you may have to share your ideas and opinions on different issues.  You will often need to support your opinions by giving reasons for what you say.
If you want to give reasons for our opinions, you can use the following expressions:
I have no doubt that you can't find them in the city because of their popularity.
There's no doubt in my mind that you can find them there.
I'm sure that you can buy the book that you can't usually buy at the bookstore.
I'm convinced that it is going to be an epic experience.
It was a great experience which I think helped me learn a lot.
I'm sure that you can see the stars that you can't usually see in the city.
I'm convinced that it's going to be an epic experience, which we will definitely remember for a long time.
There's no doubt in my mind that you are right!
You can offer reasons based on your knowledge from books, newspapers, the Internet, or any other source of information.
Example: The few stars that you can actually see are very bright in comparison to the faint ones.
